statement: Prove that if \(f\) is continuous on \([0,1]\) and \(f(x)>0\) for every \(x\in[0,1]\), then there exists \(c>0\) such that \(f(x)\ge c\) for all \(x\in[0,1]\).
Prove that if \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\) and \(f(x)\neq 0\) for all \(x\in[a,b]\), then \(f\) has the same sign on all of \([a,b]\).
Prove that if \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\) and takes only rational values, then \(f\) is constant.
Prove that if \(f\) is differentiable on \(\mathbb{R}\) and \(f'(x)>0\) for all \(x\in\mathbb{R}\), then \(f\) is one-to-one.
Prove that if \(f\) is differentiable on \(\mathbb{R}\) and \(|f'(x)|\le M\) for all \(x\), then \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le M|x-y|\) for all real \(x,y\).
Prove that if \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\) and differentiable on \((a,b)\), and if \(f'(x)\neq 0\) for all \(x\in(a,b)\), then \(f\) has at most one zero in \([a,b]\).
Prove that if \(f\) is continuous on \([0,1]\), then \(\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx=\int_0^1 f(1-x)\,dx\).
Prove that if \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\), \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=0\), and \(f(x)\ge 0\) for all \(x\), then \(f(x)=0\) for all \(x\in[a,b]\).
Prove that if \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\) and \(\int_a^b f(x)g(x)\,dx=0\) for every continuous function \(g\), then \(f(x)=0\) for all \(x\in[a,b]\).
Prove that if \(\sum a_n\) converges absolutely and \((b_n)\) is bounded, then \(\sum a_nb_n\) converges absolutely.
Prove that if a sequence \((x_n)\) is increasing and bounded above, then the sequence \((\sin x_n)\) need not be increasing, but it must have a convergent subsequence.
Prove that if a power series \(\sum c_nx^n\) converges at \(x=r>0\), then it converges absolutely for every \(x\) with \(|x|<r\).
Prove that if \(a_n\to 0\) and \((b_n)\) is bounded, then \(a_nb_n\to 0\).
Prove that if \(a_n\to L\) and \(f\) is continuous at \(L\), then \(f(a_n)\to f(L)\).
Prove that if \(f\) is continuous on \([0,1]\), then \(\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_0^1 f(x)x^n\,dx=0\).
